archimate:Principle.name: orchestration
archimate:Principle.documentation:
CONTEXT
The Integration Layer Pilot proves three patterns on Azure Integration Services and establishes repeatable standards for future delivery. It is a proof of concept and will not progress to live production.
For Orchestration, a consuming application calls a REST API through API Management (APIM), and the API returns data from the source system. The pilot uses a new read-only MOP API v1, hosted on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and secured with Entra ID OAuth 2.0, as the Orchestration Service described in the Integration Layer low-level design (v0.11). This proves that a new API can be built to HLD v4 standards, including the mandatory DSA and UK GEMINI header tags, the enterprise canonical model and standard error formats.
The live MOP database is on-premise, on Windows Server 2008 R2 behind an end-of-life firewall, and is linked to PCS, L&C and TMS. Azure Relay was rejected at the 11 November meeting, and a permanent fix does not fit in the pilot timeframe.
PROPOSAL
Use an isolated, read-only copy of the MOP Oracle database in Azure (building on the existing Azure VM copy) as the data source for MOP API v1 throughout the pilot. The copy is refreshed daily.
MOP API v1 will abstract its data access layer, so the database connection remains configurable for future reuse. The Azure copy will be decommissioned at pilot closeout (owner to be agreed).
